questions.question: Which statement is correct with reference to Neptunium?

options.text: It was known during Mendeleev’s time.
It is a naturally occurring element found in pitchblende.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It is a naturally occurring element found in pitchblende.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neptunium** is a **naturally occurring element** that is found in trace amounts in ores like **pitchblende**, a uranium-rich mineral.
 
• It is a part of the **actinide series** in the periodic table and has the atomic number **93**.
 
• Neptunium is formed as a byproduct in the decay chain of uranium and thorium, as well as during the operation of nuclear reactors.
 
• It was discovered in **1940** by Edwin McMillan and Philip Abelson at the **University of California, Berkeley.**
 
• The element is **radioactive** and has no stable isotopes. The most common isotope of Neptunium is **Neptunium-237**, which has a half-life of approximately **2.14 million years**.
 
• It is primarily used in **nuclear science** for research purposes and in the production of plutonium-238, which is used in **radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs)** for space missions.
 
• Pitchblende, also known as uraninite, is a principal ore of **uranium** and a source of Neptunium due to its trace presence.
 
• Neptunium is a **silvery metal** with properties similar to uranium and plutonium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** It is non-reactive element**__

 __
 
• Neptunium is a **reactive element**. It reacts with oxygen, acids, and halogens, contrary to the statement that it is non-reactive.
 
• It forms a variety of compounds, including **oxides and halides**, and shows multiple oxidation states ranging from +3 to +7.
 
• Its reactivity is one of the reasons for its use in chemical and nuclear research.
 
 
 
• **It is stable element**__
 __
 
• Neptunium is **radioactive** and does not have any stable isotopes, making the statement incorrect.
 
• Its isotopes decay over time through various processes such as alpha decay, beta decay, and spontaneous fission.
 
 
 
• **It was known during Mendeleev's time**__
 __
 
• Neptunium was not discovered during **Mendeleev's time**. It was only discovered in **1940**, long after Mendeleev developed the periodic table in **1869**.
 
• Mendeleev's periodic table did not include elements beyond uranium (atomic number 92), as transuranic elements like Neptunium were synthesized later.
 
 
 
• **General Information on Pitchblende**__
 
 
• **Pitchblende**, also known as uraninite, is a **black or brownish-black mineral** that is primarily composed of uranium oxide (**UO₂**).
 
• It is an important ore for extracting **uranium** and contains trace amounts of other elements like **radium, thorium, and Neptunium.**
 
• The mineral is found in countries like **Canada, Congo, the Czech Republic, and the United States.**

questions.question: According to the induced-fit model of enzyme action, substrate binding __________.

options.text: inhibits the enzyme by permanently altering its structure
induces a conformational change that optimises the active site for catalysis
occurs without any change to the enzyme’s active site
leads to immediate release of the substrate without transformation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**induces a conformational change that optimises the active site for catalysis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The induced-fit model suggests that when a substrate binds to an enzyme, **it induces a conformational change in the enzyme**, optimizing the active site for catalytic activity.
 
• This change enhances the enzyme's ability to catalyze the reaction by aligning critical amino acid residues and stabilizing the transition state.
 
• The model explains why enzymes exhibit high specificity

questions.question: Oil and fat containing food items are flushed with nitrogen because it:

options.text: Enhances the flavour of the product
Adds nutritional value to the product

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Removes oxygen from the packaging**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Nitrogen is an inert gas that is used to displace oxygen in the packaging of oil and fat-containing food items.
 
• Oxygen promotes oxidation, which can cause the food to become rancid, leading to spoilage and off-flavors.
 
• Flushing with nitrogen helps to extend the shelf life of the product by preventing oxidation and microbial growth.
 
• It maintains the freshness, taste, and nutritional quality of the food by creating a protective atmosphere.
 
• This method is commonly used in the packaging of snacks, chips, and other processed food products to ensure product integrity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation:**

 
 
• A chemical reaction involving oxygen that can degrade the quality of food, especially oils and fats.
 
• Oxidation leads to the formation of peroxides and other compounds, causing rancidity in food.
 
 
 
• **Rancidity:**
 
 
• Refers to the unpleasant smell and taste of oils or fats when they undergo oxidation.
 
• It is a major cause of spoilage in fat-containing food products.
 
 
 
• **Modified Atmosphere Packaging (MAP):**
 
 
• MAP is a technology used in food packaging where the atmosphere inside the package is altered to preserve freshness.
 
• Nitrogen flushing is a common method used in MAP to replace oxygen and increase shelf life.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen Gas:**
 
 
• It is an inert, non-reactive gas that does not support combustion or oxidation.
 
• It is widely used in food packaging to protect products from spoilage due to its inert nature.
 
 
 
• **Shelf Life:**
 
 
• The period during which a food product remains safe to consume and retains its desired sensory, chemical, and microbiological characteristics.
 
• Proper packaging, such as nitrogen flushing, plays a crucial role in extending the shelf life of food items.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: How many naturally occurring elements did the periodic law originally reveal analogies among?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**94**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The periodic law, as formulated by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869, originally revealed analogies among the **94 naturally occurring elements**.
 
• These 94 elements include hydrogen (atomic number 1) to plutonium (atomic number 94), which occur naturally on Earth.
 
• Mendeleev’s periodic table organized elements based on their **atomic masses** and chemical properties.
 
• The periodic table demonstrated repeating patterns (periodicity) of chemical properties, which helped predict the existence of undiscovered elements.
 
• Subsequent discoveries showed that **atomic number** (number of protons) is the most accurate method for organizing elements, refining the periodic law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Law:**

 
 
• States that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
 
• The modern periodic table is arranged based on atomic numbers, not atomic masses, correcting early discrepancies.
 
 
 
• **Naturally Occurring Elements:**
 
 
• Of the 118 known elements, 94 occur naturally, while the rest are synthetic.
 
• Technetium (atomic number 43) and promethium (atomic number 61) are notable exceptions that are artificial.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Trends:**
 
 
• Include properties like electronegativity, ionization energy, atomic radius, and electron affinity.
 
• These trends help predict the reactivity and bonding behavior of elements.
 
 
 
• **Discovery of New Elements:**
 
 
• Since Mendeleev’s time, new elements have been synthesized in laboratories, expanding the periodic table.
 
• Elements beyond uranium (atomic number 92) are called transuranic elements and are synthetic.

questions.question: In the reaction: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, if 5 moles of H₂ and 2 moles of O₂ are mixed, the limiting reagent is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**O₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a chemical reaction, the **limiting reagent is the reactant that is completely consumed first, limiting the amount of product formed**.
 
• The reaction provided is **2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O**, where 2 moles of H₂ react with 1 mole of O₂ to form 2 moles of water (H₂O).
 
• Given 5 moles of H₂ and 2 moles of O₂, the stoichiometric ratio is analyzed: 5 moles H₂ would require (5/2) = 2.5 moles of O₂, but only 2 moles of O₂ are available.
 
• Since O₂ is insufficient to react with all the H₂, it is the limiting reagent.
 
• The excess reactant in this scenario is H₂, as not all 5 moles of H₂ can react due to the shortage of O₂.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Limiting Reagent:**

 
 
• The reactant that determines the maximum amount of product formed in a chemical reaction.
 
• It is completely consumed during the reaction, leaving other reactants in excess.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry:**
 
 
• The quantitative relationship between reactants and products in a balanced chemical equation.
 
• It helps in determining the mole ratio required for a reaction.
 
 
 
• **Mole Concept:**
 
 
• A mole represents 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number) of a substance.
 
• Moles are used to express quantities in chemical reactions for easy stoichiometric calculations.
 
 
 
• **Excess Reagent:**
 
 
• The reactant that remains unreacted after the limiting reagent is completely consumed.
 
• In this case, H₂ is the excess reagent.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Limiting Reagent Concept:**
 
 
• Used in industrial chemical processes to optimize reactant usage.
 
• Helps prevent wastage and reduce costs by determining the exact proportions of reactants.

questions.question: In glycolysis, which enzyme catalyses the rate-limiting phosphorylation of fructose-6 phosphate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1)** is the **rate-limiting enzyme** in glycolysis, catalyzing the phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.
 
• PFK-1 is an allosteric enzyme regulated by ATP, citrate, and AMP, ensuring glycolysis responds to the cell's energy needs.
 
• This enzyme plays a critical role in controlling the flux of glucose metabolism under different physiological conditions.
 
• High levels of ATP inhibit PFK-1 activity, while AMP and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate activate it, ensuring energy production aligns with cellular demands.
 
• PFK-1 is active in the cytoplasm and is essential for anaerobic and aerobic energy production pathways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glycolysis**

 
 
• Glycolysis is a **10-step metabolic pathway that converts glucose into pyruvate**, generating ATP and NADH.
 
• It occurs in the cytoplasm of cells and is the first stage of cellular respiration.
 
• The pathway can function under both aerobic and anaerobic conditions.
 
• The primary products of glycolysis are 2 molecules of pyruvate, 2 ATP, and 2 NADH per glucose molecule.
 
 
 
• **Hexokinase**
 
 
• Hexokinase catalyzes the first step of glycolysis, converting glucose to glucose-6-phosphate.
 
• It is inhibited by its product, glucose-6-phosphate, to regulate glucose uptake.
 
 
 
• **Pyruvate Kinase**
 
 
• Pyruvate kinase catalyzes the final step of glycolysis, converting phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvate.
 
• It is regulated by fructose-1,6-bisphosphate (feed-forward activation) and ATP (inhibition).
 
 
 
• **Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate**
 
 
• This molecule is a potent activator of PFK-1, enhancing glycolysis during high energy demand.
 
• Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate is synthesized by phosphofructokinase-2 (PFK-2) in response to hormonal signals like insulin.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the use of baking soda in the kitchen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**For food colouring**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Baking soda **is primarily used in cooking as a **leavening agent**, helping baked goods rise by releasing carbon dioxide gas when combined with acidic ingredients.
 
• It is a common ingredient in **antacids**, which help neutralize stomach acid and relieve heartburn or indigestion.
 
• Baking soda is utilized in **fire extinguishers**, especially for kitchen fires, as it releases carbon dioxide to smother flames.
 
• Baking soda **does not serve as a food coloring agent**; its chemical properties are not designed for altering the color of food.
 
• Its versatility makes it useful for cooking, cleaning, and even personal care, but food coloring is not one of its applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leavening Agent:** Baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) reacts with acidic substances like vinegar or lemon juice to produce carbon dioxide, which causes dough or batter to expand and rise.
 
• **Antacid Properties:** As a mild alkaline substance, baking soda neutralizes excess stomach acid, providing relief for conditions like heartburn and acid reflux.
 
• **Fire Extinguishing Use:** Baking soda releases carbon dioxide when heated, which helps extinguish small grease fires by cutting off the oxygen supply.
 
• **Other Household Uses:** Baking soda is widely used for cleaning, deodorizing, and personal care, such as teeth whitening and skin exfoliation.
 
• **Food Coloring Agents:** Food coloring involves dyes or pigments specifically designed to alter the color of food, unlike baking soda, which has no such chemical properties.

questions.question: Which feature of the phosphodiester bond contributes most to the overall negative charge of the DNA molecule?

options.text: The phosphate group’s ionisable oxygen atoms

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The phosphate group's ionisable oxygen atoms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• DNA molecules carry a** negative charge**, primarily due to the presence of the phosphate group in the phosphodiester backbone.
 
• The phosphate group contains **ionisable oxygen atoms** that are negatively charged at physiological pH.
 
• These negatively charged oxygen atoms contribute to the **overall negative charge of the DNA molecule**, which affects its interactions with proteins, cations, and other molecules.
 
• The negative charge of DNA is critical for its **structural stability and biological functions**, such as in its interaction with histones and its electrophoretic mobility during gel-based experiments.
 
• Other components of DNA, such as the nitrogenous bases and the sugar, do not contribute significantly to the molecule's overall charge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phosphodiester Bond:**

 
 
• A phosphodiester bond is a chemical bond formed between the 3'-hydroxyl group of one sugar and the phosphate group attached to the 5'-carbon of another sugar in the DNA or RNA backbone.
 
• This bond is crucial for the formation of the DNA and RNA polymer structure.
 
 
 
• **Role of Negative Charge in DNA:**
 
 
• The negative charge on DNA facilitates its interaction with positively charged proteins such as histones, which help in DNA packaging in chromatin.
 
• It also allows the DNA to migrate towards the positive electrode during electrophoresis, a common laboratory technique for DNA analysis.
 
 
 
• **Physiological pH:**
 
 
• The ionisation of the phosphate group occurs at physiological pH (~7.4), ensuring the DNA remains negatively charged under normal biological conditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Components of DNA:**
 
 
• The nitrogenous bases (adenine, thymine, cytosine, guanine) and the deoxyribose sugar are neutral and do not contribute to the overall charge of the DNA molecule.

questions.question: What was the unknown element under aluminium called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eka-Aluminium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Eka-Aluminium** was the name given by Dmitri Mendeleev to the unknown element predicted to lie below aluminium in the periodic table.
 
• Mendeleev formulated this term based on his periodic law, where "Eka-" means "one beyond" in Sanskrit, indicating its position relative to aluminium.
 
• The element later discovered and identified as Eka-Aluminium is **Gallium (Ga)**, which was found in 1875 by French chemist Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran.
 
• Mendeleev accurately predicted various properties of Eka-Aluminium, including its atomic mass, density, melting point, and oxide formula.
 
• The discovery of Gallium validated Mendeleev’s periodic table and his concept of periodicity, strengthening the scientific acceptance of the table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Law:**

 
 
• Mendeleev's periodic law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses.
 
• This law formed the basis for the organization of elements in the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Gallium:**
 
 
• Gallium has an atomic number of 31 and is a soft, silvery metal.
 
• It melts at a low temperature of about 29.76°C, making it unique among metals.
 
• Gallium is used in semiconductors, LEDs, and solar panels.
 
 
 
• **Mendeleev's Predictions:**
 
 
• Mendeleev predicted the existence and properties of several elements that were unknown at the time, including Scandium (Eka-Boron), Gallium (Eka-Aluminium), and Germanium (Eka-Silicon).
 
• His predictions were based on gaps in his periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Validation of Periodic Table:**
 
 
• The discovery of elements like Gallium, which matched Mendeleev's predictions, confirmed the accuracy and utility of the periodic table.
 
• This established the periodic table as one of the most important tools in chemistry.

questions.question: In acidic medium, the balanced redox reaction for MnO₄⁻ + Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + Fe³⁺ is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The balanced redox reaction in acidic medium is: **MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O**.
 
• In this reaction, **MnO₄⁻** is reduced to **Mn²⁺**, and Fe²⁺ is oxidized to Fe³⁺.
 
• Manganese in MnO₄⁻ undergoes a change in oxidation state from **+7 to +2**, indicating a reduction process.
 
• Iron in Fe²⁺ undergoes a change in oxidation state from **+2 to +3**, indicating an oxidation process.
 
• The presence of **H⁺ ions** (acidic medium) is crucial for balancing the reaction and ensuring proper electron transfer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Permanganate Ion (MnO₄⁻):**

 
 
• It is a strong oxidizing agent and plays a significant role in redox reactions.
 
• In acidic medium, MnO₄⁻ is reduced to Mn²⁺, while in basic medium, it is reduced to MnO₂.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation and Reduction:**
 
 
• Oxidation involves the loss of electrons, whereas reduction involves the gain of electrons.
 
• In this reaction, Fe²⁺ loses one electron (oxidation), and MnO₄⁻ gains five electrons (reduction).
 
 
 
• **Balancing Redox Reactions:**
 
 
• Redox reactions are balanced by ensuring both mass and charge are conserved.
 
• In acidic medium, H⁺ ions are used to balance the reaction alongside water molecules.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Redox Chemistry:**
 
 
• Redox reactions are widely used in industries for processes like electroplating, corrosion prevention, and chemical synthesis.
 
• Permanganate titrations are commonly used for determining the concentration of reducing agents in analytical chemistry.

questions.question: Which unique property of Plasmodium makes malaria a cyclical disease with periodic fever?

options.text: RBC rupture and toxin release every few days

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RBC rupture and toxin release every few days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The periodic fever in malaria is caused by the synchronous rupture of infected red blood cells (RBCs) and the release of toxins, primarily **hemozoin pigment and other inflammatory mediators**, into the bloodstream.
 
• Plasmodium parasites undergo a complex life cycle, including asexual reproduction within RBCs, leading to their destruction every 48-72 hours depending on the species.
 
• The cyclical nature of fever corresponds to the completion of the parasite's schizogony stage within RBCs, which is synchronized across a population of parasites.
 
• Species-specific periodicity: Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale cause fever every 48 hours, while Plasmodium malariae causes it every 72 hours, and Plasmodium falciparum often exhibits irregular fever patterns.
 
• The toxins and metabolites released during RBC rupture trigger immune responses, including the release of cytokines like **tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α)**, leading to fever and other systemic symptoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasmodium Life Cycle:**

 
 
• The life cycle involves two hosts: humans and female Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• In humans, Plasmodium first infects liver cells (exo-erythrocytic stage) and then moves to RBCs (erythrocytic stage).
 
 
 
• **Hemozoin:**
 
 
• A toxic byproduct of hemoglobin metabolism by Plasmodium parasites.
 
• Hemozoin accumulation is a key factor in triggering immune responses and systemic inflammation.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Fever Mechanism:**
 
 
• Caused by synchronized schizont rupture and immune system activation.
 
• Cytokines like TNF-α and interleukin-1 (IL-1) are released, leading to fever.
 
 
 
• **Plasmodium Species:**
 
 
• Four major human-infecting species: P. vivax, P. ovale, P. malariae, and P. falciparum.
 
• P. falciparum is the most dangerous, often causing severe and complicated malaria.
 
 
 
• **Malaria Transmission:**
 
 
• Spread via bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• Control measures include insecticide-treated bed nets and antimalarial drugs.

questions.question: Which major discovery helps to design drugs in the treatment of hyperacidity?

options.text: The role of enzymes in digestion
The use of antibiotics to neutralize stomach acid
Hydrochloric acid present in the stomach
Histamine stimulates acid secretion in the stomach

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Histamine stimulates acid secretion in the stomach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Histamine plays a crucial role** in stimulating the secretion of gastric acid in the stomach by binding to H2 receptors on the parietal cells.
 
• This discovery has been instrumental in the development of **H2 receptor antagonists** such as ranitidine and famotidine, which are widely used to treat hyperacidity and related disorders.
 
• Histamine-mediated acid secretion is an important target in the treatment of conditions like **gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcers, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome**.
 
• The regulation of histamine pathways has also led to advancements in **proton pump inhibitors (PPIs)**, which further reduce gastric acid production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Histamine:** A chemical messenger released by certain cells in the body, including mast cells, that plays a key role in immune responses and gastric acid secretion.
 
• **H2 Receptor Antagonists:** Drugs like ranitidine and cimetidine that block histamine H2 receptors, reducing stomach acid production and relieving symptoms of hyperacidity.
 
• **Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs):** Medications such as omeprazole and esomeprazole that inhibit the final step in acid secretion, providing long-lasting relief for acid-related conditions.
 
• **Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD):** A chronic condition where stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus, causing irritation and requiring acid-suppressing treatments.
 
• **Parietal Cells:** Specialized cells in the stomach lining that produce hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor, essential for digestion and vitamin B12 absorption.

questions.question: What is the formula for density?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Density = Mass / Volume**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Density** is defined as the amount of mass per unit volume of a substance.
 
• The standard formula for density is **Density = Mass / Volume**.
 
• The SI unit of density is **kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m³)**.
 
• Density helps determine whether a substance will **sink or float** when placed in a fluid.
 
• Commonly used in various fields, including physics, chemistry, and engineering, to analyze material properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass:** The quantity of matter in an object, measured in kilograms (kg) in the SI system.
 
• **Volume:** The amount of space occupied by an object or substance, measured in cubic meters (m³) in the SI system.
 
• **Relative Density:** It is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of a reference substance (usually water for liquids and solids).
 
• **Buoyancy:** An object's ability to float is determined by comparing its density to the density of the fluid it is placed in.
 
• Materials with higher density than water (1 g/cm³) will sink, whereas those with lower density will float.

questions.question: Why is the discovery of penicillin considered revolutionary in medicine?

options.text: It was used for colouring bacteria.
It treated pain rather than infections
It was used only in animals.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It began the antibiotic era**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The discovery of **penicillin** is considered a revolutionary event in the field of medicine because it marked the beginning of the **antibiotic era**.
 
• Penicillin was discovered by **Alexander Fleming** in **1928** when he observed that the fungus **Penicillium notatum** inhibited the growth of bacteria.
 
• It was the first naturally occurring **antibiotic** to be discovered and introduced for clinical use.
 
• Penicillin drastically changed the treatment of bacterial infections like **pneumonia, syphilis, strep throat, and wound infections**, saving millions of lives.
 
• Its introduction significantly reduced the mortality rate from infectious diseases, which were previously a leading cause of death.
 
• The success of penicillin paved the way for the discovery and development of other antibiotics, transforming the field of medicine and public health.
 
• During **World War II**, penicillin was mass-produced and used to treat soldiers, further proving its effectiveness and importance.
 
• It is considered one of the most important medical discoveries of the **20th century** and has been instrumental in controlling infections globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It was used for colouring bacteria**__

 __
 
• Penicillin was not used for colouring bacteria. However, in microbiology, certain **dyes** like crystal violet and methylene blue are commonly used for staining bacteria to observe their structure.
 
 
 
• **It treated pain rather than infections**__
 __
 
• This is incorrect because penicillin is an **antibiotic**, which means it is used to treat bacterial infections, not pain. Painkillers like **aspirin** or **paracetamol** are used to manage pain.
 
 
 
• **It was used only in animals**__
 
 
• Penicillin was first tested on **animals** to ensure its safety, but its primary use has been for **humans**. Later, it was also used in veterinary medicine to treat bacterial infections in animals.

questions.question: The Michaelis-Menten constant (Km) of an enzyme is defined as:

options.text: The enzyme concentration required for half-maximal catalysis
The inhibtori concentration that reduces enzyme activity by 50%
The substrate concentration at which the reaction rate is half of Vmax

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The substrate concentration at which the reaction rate is half of Vmax.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Michaelis-Menten constant (Km)** is a crucial parameter in enzyme kinetics, often used to describe the efficiency of an enzyme in catalyzing reactions.
 
• **Km** is defined as the **substrate concentration** at which the enzyme-catalyzed reaction rate is **half of Vmax** (maximum reaction rate).
 
• This constant reflects the enzyme's **affinity for its substrate**. A **low Km** value indicates a **high affinity**, meaning the enzyme works efficiently even at low substrate concentrations.
 
• Conversely, a **high Km** value suggests a **lower affinity**, requiring higher substrate concentrations for effective catalysis.
 
• The Michaelis-Menten equation, **v = (Vmax[S]) / (Km + [S])**, relates the reaction rate (**v**) to substrate concentration (**[S]**), Vmax, and Km.
 
• The concept is widely applied in biochemistry and molecular biology to study enzyme behavior and design inhibitors for therapeutic purposes.
 
• This parameter is particularly relevant for understanding enzyme function in different physiological and pathological contexts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The enzyme concentration required for half-maximal catalysis**__

 __
 
• The term refers to the amount of enzyme needed for half-maximal reaction but is not related to the definition of **Km**. Km depends on substrate concentration, not enzyme concentration.
 
 
 
• **The maximum reaction rate (Vmax)**__
 __
 
• **Vmax** is the highest reaction rate achieved when the enzyme is saturated with substrate. While Km is tied to Vmax, it does not describe the reaction rate itself.
 
 
 
• **The inhibitor concentration that reduces enzyme activity by 50%**__
 
 
• This concept is related to **IC50** (Inhibitory Concentration 50), which is different from Km. IC50 is used to measure inhibitor potency rather than substrate affinity.

questions.question: Which group did iodine belong to in Mendeleev’s table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Group VII**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iodine** belongs to **Group VII** in **Mendeleev’s periodic table**, which is the group of halogens.
 
• Mendeleev’s periodic table was arranged based on the **atomic mass** of elements, and elements with similar properties were placed in the same group.
 
• Group VII in Mendeleev's table includes elements like **fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine,** and **astatine**.
 
• Halogens are known for their strong reactivity and their ability to form salts when combined with metals.
 
• **Iodine** is a **non-metallic element** and is known for its role in the synthesis of **thyroid hormones** in the human body.
 
• Mendeleev predicted the properties of elements that were not discovered during his time and left gaps in his periodic table for them.
 
• The placement of iodine in Group VII was based on its properties aligning with other halogens, despite slight inconsistencies in atomic mass trends.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Group VIII**__

 __
 
• Group VIII in Mendeleev's table includes elements like **iron, cobalt,** and **nickel**.
 
• These elements are **transition metals** and are known for their ability to form alloys and their magnetic properties.
 
 
 
• **Group V**__
 __
 
• Group V includes elements such as **nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, antimony,** and **bismuth**.
 
• These elements exhibit a wide range of properties, from non-metals (like nitrogen) to metalloids (like arsenic) and metals (like bismuth).
 
 
 
• **Group VI**__
 
 
• Group VI includes elements such as **oxygen, sulfur, selenium, tellurium,** and **polonium**.
 
• These elements are known as **chalcogens** and are essential for various biological and industrial processes.

questions.question: Which bacterial disease is specifically confirmed by a serological method?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Typhoid**__.

*__Key Points__

__
 
• **Typhoid** is a bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi*, which spreads through contaminated food and water.
 
• The disease is commonly diagnosed using the **Widal test**, a serological test that detects antibodies against *S. typhi* antigens.
 
• The Widal test evaluates the presence of **O (somatic) and H (flagellar) antigens** in the blood, which are specific to typhoid fever.
 
• This method is preferred in areas with limited access to advanced diagnostic tools and is widely used for diagnosing typhoid in endemic regions.
 
• While the Widal test is widely used, its results must be interpreted cautiously alongside the patient’s clinical history and other diagnostic findings.

***Additional Information__**

 
• **Widal Test:**

 
 
• Developed in 1896 by Georges-Fernand Widal, it remains one of the most common methods to diagnose typhoid fever.
 
• A fourfold increase in antibody titers in two consecutive samples taken 7–10 days apart confirms the diagnosis of typhoid.
 
• False-positive results may occur due to previous infections or vaccination with S. typhi*.
 
 
 
• **Other Diagnostic Methods for Typhoid:**
 
 
• Blood Culture: The most reliable method, especially in the early stages of the disease.
 
• Bone Marrow Culture: Considered the most sensitive diagnostic method but is invasive and rarely used.
 
• Typhidot Test: A rapid diagnostic test that detects IgM and IgG antibodies specific to typhoid.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms of Typhoid:**
 
 
• High fever, abdominal pain, weakness, headache, loss of appetite, and constipation or diarrhea.
 
• In severe cases, it can lead to intestinal perforation and sepsis.
 
 
 
• **Prevention of Typhoid:**
 
 
• Vaccination: Typhoid conjugate vaccines and oral live-attenuated vaccines are available.
 
• Ensure safe drinking water, proper sanitation, and hygiene to prevent transmission.

questions.question: What is the temperature of the triple point of water on the Celsius scale?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.01ºC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The triple point of water is the temperature and pressure at which water exists simultaneously in its **solid, liquid, and gaseous states**.
 
• On the Celsius scale, the triple point of water is precisely **0.01ºC**.
 
• This value is used as a standard fixed point in the definition of the Celsius temperature scale.
 
• The corresponding pressure at the triple point of water is exactly **611.657 pascals (Pa)**.
 
• The triple point of water is critical for scientific calibration of thermometers and maintaining the International Temperature Scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Triple Point:**

 
 
• The triple point is a unique thermodynamic state where three phases (solid, liquid, and gas) coexist in equilibrium.
 
• It is a fundamental reference point for thermodynamic measurements.
 
 
 
• **Kelvin and Celsius Relationship:**
 
 
• The triple point of water is defined as 273.16 K on the Kelvin scale.
 
• The Celsius scale is defined such that the triple point of water is 0.01ºC.
 
 
 
• **Role in Metrology:**
 
 
• The triple point of water is used in metrology to calibrate temperature-measuring instruments.
 
• It is a key reference point for defining the International Temperature Scale (ITS-90).
 
 
 
• **Physical Significance:**
 
 
• The triple point demonstrates the delicate balance of thermodynamic states under specific conditions.
 
• For water, it highlights the unique properties of this universal solvent, which is critical for life on Earth.

questions.question: What happens to magnetic fields when a material becomes superconducting and experiences the Meissner effect?

options.text: Magnetic fields are completely expelled from the interior of the material.
Magnetic fields penetrate the material freely.
Magnetic fields are increased in strength within the material.
Magnetic fields are absorbed and stored inside the material.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnetic fields are completely expelled from the interior of the material.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Meissner effect is a defining property of superconductors where magnetic fields are expelled from the interior of the material during the transition to the superconducting state.
 
• This phenomenon occurs below a critical temperature (Tc) unique to each superconducting material.
 
• The expulsion of magnetic fields is a result of the superconducting material forming perfect diamagnetic properties.
 
• As the superconducting state is achieved, the material cancels the internal magnetic field by generating surface currents that oppose the applied magnetic field.
 
• It is distinct from perfect conductivity, as it implies both zero electrical resistance and zero magnetic field within the material.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Superconductivity:**

 
 
• Superconductivity is a quantum mechanical phenomenon where certain materials exhibit zero electrical resistance and expel magnetic fields below a critical temperature.
 
• It was discovered in 1911 by Heike Kamerlingh Onnes in mercury cooled to 4.2 K.
 
• Applications include MRI machines, particle accelerators, and quantum computing.
 
 
 
• **Meissner Effect:**
 
 
• Named after Walther Meissner and Robert Ochsenfeld, who discovered it in 1933.
 
• It demonstrates the fundamental difference between superconductors and perfect conductors.
 
• The magnetic field is expelled entirely from the bulk of the material, not just reduced.
 
 
 
• **Type I vs Type II Superconductors:**
 
 
• Type I superconductors completely expel magnetic fields and are typically elemental metals.
 
• Type II superconductors allow partial penetration of magnetic fields in the form of vortices and are often alloys or compounds.
 
 
 
• **Critical Temperature (Tc):**
 
 
• The temperature below which a material becomes superconducting.
 
• Varies widely among materials, from below 1 K in some metals to above 100 K in high-temperature superconductors.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency is most likely in a person with a blocked bile duct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A blocked bile duct impairs the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, which include **Vitamins A, D, E, and K**.
 
• Vitamin A deficiency is more likely as it is a fat-soluble vitamin requiring bile for proper absorption.
 
• Vitamin A plays a crucial role in maintaining healthy vision, immune function, and skin integrity.
 
• A lack of bile prevents the emulsification of dietary fats, thereby reducing the bioavailability of fat-soluble vitamins like Vitamin A.
 
• Symptoms of Vitamin A deficiency include night blindness, dry eyes (xerophthalmia), and increased susceptibility to infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bile Duct Function:** The bile duct transports bile, which is essential for the digestion and absorption of dietary fats and fat-soluble vitamins.
 
• **Fat-Soluble Vitamins:** These include Vitamins A, D, E, and K, which are stored in the liver and fatty tissues and are absorbed along with dietary fats.
 
• **Vitamin A Sources:** Dietary sources include liver, fish oils, dairy products, and colorful fruits and vegetables (e.g., carrots, spinach, and sweet potatoes).
 
• **Other Fat-Soluble Vitamin Deficiencies:** A blocked bile duct can also lead to deficiencies in Vitamins D (affecting bone health), E (antioxidant function), and K (blood clotting).
 
• **Clinical Management:** Patients with bile duct obstruction may require supplementation of fat-soluble vitamins in water-soluble forms to prevent deficiencies.

questions.question: Which of the following elements had NOT been discovered during Mendeleev’s time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radon and Polonium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During Mendeleev's time (late 19th century), the periodic table was incomplete, and many elements were yet to be discovered.
 
• **Radon** (Rn) is a noble gas discovered much later in 1900 by Friedrich Ernst Dorn. It was absent from Mendeleev's periodic table.
 
• **Polonium** (Po) was discovered in 1898 by Marie and Pierre Curie, a few decades after Mendeleev's initial work on the periodic table.
 
• Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table for elements he predicted but had not yet been discovered. Radon and Polonium were not among the elements he predicted.
 
• In contrast, elements like Hydrogen, Nitrogen, Chlorine, and Fluorine were well-known during Mendeleev's time and incorporated into his periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mendeleev's Periodic Table**:

 
 
• Proposed in 1869 by Dmitri Mendeleev, it was based on atomic mass and properties of elements.
 
• He left gaps for elements that were not discovered yet, predicting their properties with remarkable accuracy.
 
• Gallium (discovered in 1875) and Germanium (discovered in 1886) were among the elements predicted by Mendeleev.
 
 
 
• **Noble Gases**:
 
 
• Noble gases like Radon were not part of Mendeleev's table because they were discovered later and required the addition of a new group in the periodic table.
 
• The group of noble gases was added after the discovery of Helium and Argon in the late 19th century.
 
 
 
• **Polonium**:
 
 
• A radioactive element discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie in 1898 while studying pitchblende.
 
• It was named after Poland, Marie Curie's homeland.
 
 
 
• **Radon**:
 
 
• Radon is a radioactive noble gas, discovered as a decay product of radium.
 
• It is colorless, odorless, and chemically inert, making its detection challenging initially.
 
 
 
• **Modern Periodic Table**:
 
 
• Organized by atomic number rather than atomic mass, as proposed by Henry Moseley in 1913.
 
• This resolved inconsistencies in Mendeleev's table, especially for elements like Argon and Potassium.

questions.question: Which component is commonly used in a circuit to vary the resistance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rheostat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **rheostat** is a variable resistor used in electrical circuits to adjust the resistance.
 
• It is commonly used to control the flow of current in a circuit and thus regulate voltage or power.
 
• Rheostats are constructed with a resistive wire wound around an insulating core, allowing for resistance adjustment by moving a slider or wiper.
 
• They are widely utilized in applications such as dimming lights, controlling motor speed, and tuning radios.
 
• Unlike fixed resistors, rheostats offer the flexibility of altering resistance dynamically during operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistor:** A passive electrical component that provides resistance to control current in a circuit. Fixed resistors have a set resistance value, unlike variable resistors like rheostats.
 
• **Potentiometer:** Another variable resistor, similar to a rheostat but typically used for measuring or dividing voltage rather than controlling current directly.
 
• **Ohm’s Law:** The fundamental principle governing the relationship between voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R) in an electrical circuit, represented by the equation V = IR.
 
• **Applications of Rheostats:** Besides light dimming and motor control, rheostats are used in experimental setups to test circuits and components under varying resistance conditions.
 
• **Difference Between Rheostat and Transformer:** While a rheostat alters resistance to control current, a transformer is an electrical device that changes voltage levels through electromagnetic induction.

questions.question: What is the function of subsidiary cells?

options.text: Support of guard cells in stomatal function
Secretion of enzymes for nutrient acquisition, defence and digestion

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Support of guard cells in stomatal function**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Subsidiary cells are specialized epidermal cells that are associated with guard cells and help in stomatal function.
 
• They play an indirect role in regulating the opening and closing of stomata by providing mechanical support to guard cells.
 
• Subsidiary cells contribute to maintaining the ion balance and turgor pressure required for guard cells to function effectively.
 
• These cells are part of the stomatal complex, which is crucial for gas exchange and transpiration in plants.
 
• The presence of subsidiary cells varies among plant species and is a characteristic feature used for plant identification.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stomata:**

 
 
• Stomata are microscopic pores present on the surface of leaves and stems that facilitate gas exchange (CO2 intake and O2 release).
 
• They are surrounded by guard cells, which regulate their opening and closing based on environmental conditions.
 
 
 
• **Guard Cells:**
 
 
• Guard cells are specialized cells that control the size of the stomatal pore by changing their shape.
 
• They respond to factors like light, water availability, and internal CO2 concentration.
 
 
 
• **Subsidiary Cells:**
 
 
• Subsidiary cells are part of the epidermis and surround guard cells, forming the stomatal complex.
 
• They vary in shape, size, and arrangement depending on the plant species.
 
 
 
• **Function of Stomatal Complex:**
 
 
• Facilitates transpiration and cooling of the plant.
 
• Plays a key role in photosynthesis by enabling CO2 uptake.
 
• Helps maintain the plant's water balance by regulating water loss.

questions.question: A gas stove flame burns blue because of:

options.text: Presence of hydrogen in the air

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Complete combustion of fuel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The blue flame of a gas stove indicates **complete combustion of fuel**, which occurs when the fuel burns efficiently with a sufficient oxygen supply.
 
• Complete combustion results in the production of **carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water vapor (H₂O)**, without releasing harmful gases like carbon monoxide (CO).
 
• A blue flame is a sign of **optimal energy efficiency**, as the fuel is fully utilized without wastage.
 
• Incomplete combustion, on the other hand, produces a yellow or orange flame and may release pollutants like **carbon monoxide (CO)**.
 
• Blue flames are common when burning fuels like **natural gas, propane, or butane**, which are hydrocarbons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Complete Combustion:** A chemical process where a fuel reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water, and energy. It requires a sufficient oxygen supply.
 
• **Incomplete Combustion:** Occurs when there is insufficient oxygen, leading to the production of harmful by-products such as carbon monoxide and soot.
 
• **Hydrocarbons:** Organic compounds consisting of hydrogen and carbon atoms. Common fuels like natural gas and propane are hydrocarbons.
 
• **Carbon Monoxide (CO):** A toxic gas produced during incomplete combustion. It is colorless, odorless, and can pose serious health risks.
 
• **Energy Efficiency:** Blue flames are an indicator of efficient energy usage, as the fuel is completely burned without wasting resources.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with reference to the industrial use of freon?

options.text: It is used in refrigeration and aerosol production.
It is primarily used in food processing and as a food preservative
It is used as a pesticide and insecticide.
It is used for textile dyeing.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is used in refrigeration and aerosol production.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Freon** is a trade name for a group of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and related compounds primarily used as refrigerants.
 
• It is widely used in **refrigeration systems** such as air conditioners, refrigerators, and freezers.
 
• Freon is also used in the production of **aerosol propellants** due to its ability to maintain pressure and flow consistency.
 
• The use of Freon has been regulated under international agreements like the **Montreal Protocol** due to its contribution to ozone layer depletion.
 
• Modern refrigeration systems are transitioning to alternative, eco-friendly refrigerants to replace Freon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs):**

 
 
• CFCs are compounds made up of chlorine, fluorine, and carbon atoms.
 
• They were once widely used in refrigeration, air conditioning, and aerosol sprays.
 
• CFCs are known to cause **ozone depletion** in the stratosphere.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol:**
 
 
• An international treaty signed in 1987 to phase out substances that deplete the ozone layer, including CFCs.
 
• The treaty has been highly successful in reducing the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Freon:**
 
 
• Freon contributes to global warming and ozone layer depletion.
 
• Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) and hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) are transitional substitutes but are also being phased out due to environmental concerns.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Refrigerants:**
 
 
• Eco-friendly refrigerants like ammonia (NH₃), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and hydrocarbons (e.g., isobutane) are being adopted.
 
• These alternatives have a lower global warming potential (GWP) and no ozone depletion potential (ODP).

questions.question: What is the primary reason that roughage is included in a balanced human diet?

options.text: It aids digestion and prevents constipation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It aids digestion and prevents constipation.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Roughage, also known as dietary fiber, is essential for **maintaining healthy bowel movements** by adding bulk to stool and preventing constipation.
 
• It promotes the growth of **healthy gut bacteria**, which aids digestion and supports overall gut health.
 
• Roughage helps in **regulating blood sugar levels** by slowing down the absorption of glucose in the bloodstream.
 
• Including adequate fiber in the diet reduces the risk of **digestive disorders**, such as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
 
• A diet rich in roughage also contributes to **long-term heart health** by lowering cholesterol levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Dietary Fiber:**

 
 
• **Soluble fiber:** Dissolves in water and forms a gel-like substance, helping to lower cholesterol and glucose levels. Found in oats, fruits, and legumes.
 
• **Insoluble fiber:** Does not dissolve in water and aids in adding bulk to stool, preventing constipation. Found in whole grains, nuts, and vegetables.
 
 
 
• **Recommended Intake:** The daily recommended intake of dietary fiber is **25 grams for women** and **38 grams for men**, as per dietary guidelines.
 
• **Health Benefits:** Fiber-rich foods help in reducing the risk of chronic diseases such as **type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and colorectal cancer**.
 
• **Sources of Roughage:** Common sources include **whole grains, fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds, and legumes**.
 
• **Role in Weight Management:** Foods high in fiber increase satiety, helping in **controlling appetite** and supporting weight management.

questions.question: In the balanced reaction 2Al + 3Cl₂ → 2AlCl₃, what is the mole ratio of aluminium to aluminium chloride?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: 2 : 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is: **2Al + 3Cl₂ → 2AlCl₃**.
 
• In the reaction, **two moles of aluminium (Al)** react with **three moles of chlorine gas (Cl₂)** to produce **two moles of aluminium chloride (AlCl₃).**
 
• The mole ratio of aluminium (Al) to aluminium chloride (AlCl₃) is **2:2**, which simplifies to **1:1**.
 
• This ratio indicates that for every two moles of aluminium, two moles of aluminium chloride are formed.
 
• The correct option is **Option 1: 2 : 2**, as it directly reflects the stoichiometric coefficients in the balanced equation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stoichiometry**: The branch of chemistry that deals with the quantitative relationships between reactants and products in a chemical reaction.
 
• **Mole Ratio**: Derived from the coefficients of the balanced chemical equation and represents the proportional relationship between substances involved in the reaction.
 
• **Balanced Equation**: Ensures the conservation of mass, where the number of atoms for each element is the same on both sides of the equation.
 
• **Reaction Details**: Aluminium reacts with chlorine gas to form aluminium chloride, an ionic compound commonly used in chemical synthesis and industrial processes.
 
• **Limiting Reactant Concept**: In practical scenarios, the reactant present in a lower stoichiometric quantity may limit the amount of product formed, but this does not affect the mole ratio derived from the balanced equation.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms exhibits both autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Euglena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Euglena** is a unique single-celled organism that exhibits both autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition.
 
• In the presence of sunlight, Euglena performs **photosynthesis** using chlorophyll, making it autotrophic.
 
• In the absence of sunlight, Euglena can obtain nutrition heterotrophically by **absorbing organic matter** from its environment.
 
• Euglena belongs to the kingdom **Protista** and is often studied as an example of a mixotrophic organism.
 
• This dual nutritional capability enables Euglena to survive in a variety of habitats, making it highly adaptable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Autotrophic Nutrition:**

 
 
• It refers to the mode of nutrition where organisms synthesize their own food using simple inorganic substances like carbon dioxide and water.
 
• Photosynthesis, using sunlight, is the most common method of autotrophic nutrition.
 
• Examples include plants, algae, and some bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Heterotrophic Nutrition:**
 
 
• In this mode, organisms depend on other organisms for food.
 
• Heterotrophs are unable to synthesize their own food and rely on consuming organic matter.
 
• Examples include animals, fungi, and certain protists like Amoeba.
 
 
 
• **Mixotrophic Nutrition:**
 
 
• Organisms like Euglena that can switch between autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition exhibit mixotrophic nutrition.
 
• This ability provides flexibility and survival advantages in fluctuating environmental conditions.
 
 
 
• **Kingdom Protista:**
 
 
• It includes a diverse group of eukaryotic organisms that are primarily unicellular.
 
• Protists can be autotrophic, heterotrophic, or mixotrophic.
 
• Examples include Euglena, Amoeba, and Paramecium.

questions.question: What is the primary industrial process of producing phenol worldwide, and what is the intermediate used in this process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cumene process, cumene hydroperoxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Cumene process, also known as the Hock process, is the most widely used industrial method for producing phenol globally.
 
• The process involves the oxidation of cumene (isopropylbenzene) to form cumene hydroperoxide as an intermediate.
 
• Cumene hydroperoxide is then cleaved to produce phenol and acetone as major products.
 
• This method is preferred due to its economic efficiency and the simultaneous production of acetone, which is a valuable byproduct.
 
• The process is primarily conducted in large-scale petrochemical plants and is used extensively in the production of plastics, resins, and other industrial materials.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cumene (Isopropylbenzene):**

 
 
• Cumene is an organic compound derived from benzene and propylene.
 
• It serves as the precursor for the production of phenol and acetone via the Cumene process.
 
• Its synthesis involves Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with propylene.
 
 
 
• **Phenol:**
 
 
• Phenol is an aromatic organic compound with the molecular formula C₆H₅OH.
 
• It is widely used in the production of plastics, resins, and other industrial chemicals such as bisphenol A.
 
• Phenol is also utilized in pharmaceuticals, dyes, and antiseptics.
 
 
 
• **Acetone:**
 
 
• Acetone (CH₃COCH₃) is a colorless, volatile solvent and a major byproduct of the Cumene process.
 
• It is commonly used in the production of acrylic plastics and as a solvent in various industries.
 
• Acetone is also used in household applications like nail polish removers.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Importance of the Cumene Process:**
 
 
• The Cumene process accounts for the majority of phenol production globally due to its cost-effectiveness.
 
• The co-production of acetone enhances the economic feasibility of the process.
 
• Advancements in catalyst technology have improved the efficiency and environmental sustainability of the process.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the shape of a sinusoidal wave signal during one complete cycle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**S-shaped wave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A sinusoidal wave signal completes one cycle in a characteristic smooth, oscillatory motion resembling an **S-shaped curve**.
 
• Sinusoidal waves are represented mathematically as **y = A sin(ωt + φ)**, where A is the amplitude, ω is the angular frequency, and φ is the phase.
 
• The wave transitions smoothly between its maximum and minimum values, creating a symmetrical **S-shape** over one complete cycle.
 
• Sinusoidal waves are fundamental in physics, engineering, and mathematics due to their periodic and harmonic nature.
 
• Such waves are commonly used in **AC electrical signals**, sound waves, and other oscillatory systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amplitude:**

 
 
• The maximum displacement of the wave from its mean position.
 
• Represents the strength or intensity of the wave.
 
 
 
• **Frequency:**
 
 
• The number of cycles completed per second, measured in Hertz (Hz).
 
• Higher frequency corresponds to faster oscillations.
 
 
 
• **Phase:**
 
 
• Defines the offset of the wave relative to a reference point.
 
• Critical for understanding wave interference and synchronization.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sinusoidal Waves:**
 
 
• Used in alternating current (AC) electricity supply systems.
 
• Fundamental to sound wave analysis and signal processing.
 
• Critical in studying harmonic motion in physics and engineering.
 
 
 
• **Wave Equation:**
 
 
• A sinusoidal wave can be expressed as y = A sin(2πft + φ).
 
• This equation helps model real-world oscillatory phenomena.
